title: Lie algebra is the cotangent dual at the rational identity
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $G$ a group scheme over $k$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Put $e=e_G(\operatorname{Spec}k)$, $R=\mathcal O_{G,e}$, and $\kappa=\kappa(e)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There exists a ring isomorphism $r:k\simeq\kappa$ and an $r$-semilinear equivalence from $\operatorname{Lie}(G)$ [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation] to $\operatorname{Hom}_\kappa(\mathfrak m_R/\mathfrak m_R^2,\kappa)$, with the canonical residue-field scalar structure on the cotangent space [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality]. No smoothness or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Dimension paragraph, identification of Lie algebra with tangent space at the identity; sk-i-cartier third paragraph; Stacks Project Tag 0B2C

proof.text: The identity section is a rational point: its equation e composed with p equals id makes the structural residue-field homomorphism k to kappa(e) bijective. Indeed the residue map back along the section is injective as a field homomorphism and its composite with the structural map is id. Take the associated ring equivalence r.

Use lieEquiv to identify the sheaf-defined Lie algebra with infinitesimal group points. Transport dual numbers from k to kappa(e) by r; the restriction-to-the-identity condition is exactly the definition of tangent vectors at e. lieEquiv_mul and toLie_infPointsScale identify addition and scalar multiplication.

Apply rational tangent-cotangent duality at e (with the identity morphism of G) to identify tangent vectors with the k-linear dual of m/m squared. Transport the functional values through r to get the kappa(e)-linear dual. The inverse transports values back through r inverse; the two are mutually inverse and compatible with scalars, yielding the semilinear equivalence. This works without smoothness or any finite-dimensional hypothesis. Explicitly subtract the structural scalar lift of the residue of a before applying the functional to its maximal-ideal class; the product formula modulo m squared gives the Leibniz rule. The unit laws make the differential of multiplication the sum of the two vectors, and epsilon scaling agrees with scalar multiplication.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_lie_identity_cotangent_dual_equiv
    {k : Type u} [Field k] (G : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GrpObj G] :
    let R := G.left.presheaf.stalk (unitSection G (IsLocalRing.closedPoint k))
    ∃ r : k ≃+* IsLocalRing.ResidueField R,
      letI : RingHomInvPair r.toRingHom r.symm.toRingHom :=
        RingHomInvPair.of_ringEquiv r
      letI : RingHomInvPair r.symm.toRingHom r.toRingHom :=
        RingHomInvPair.of_ringEquiv r.symm
      Nonempty (Lie G ≃ₛₗ[r.toRingHom]
        Module.Dual (IsLocalRing.ResidueField R) (IsLocalRing.CotangentSpace R))
